messages:
incident-bot: [CRITICAL] GPU inference queue growth detected on us-west-2 cluster 'redwood-gpu-1'. QPS spiked, queue depth > 12k, autoscaler failed to provision additional nodes (rate-limited). Auto paging to #incidents.
Sara (SRE): paging in. I see the alert, grabbing the on-call. Initial hypothesis: sudden workload spike + batching param change earlier tonight.
oncall_tier1: I'm on it. Observed token-level throttling and steady rise in pending requests. pinging infra and runtime.
Mike (Infra): seeing scale-controller errors: "scale request refused: max_nodes_limit_reached (customer quota)" and some 403s from cloud API. Also a flurry of failed node creations 1716317923 -> 1716318120.
Jonah (Runtime Eng): logs show continuous-batching latency parameter lowered in the deploy at 1716309000: `max_batch_delay_ms: 80` -> `20`. That reduces batching effectiveness for long-tail requests. Also prefix-cache missrate shot from 3% -> 58%.
Aisha (ML Eng): prefix-cache TTL was rolled forward to 3s as an experiment in the same deploy. With high concurrency that TTL is too short; we're losing KV cache locality which explodes decoder compute.
Sara (SRE): TL;DR: two config changes made the system need more GPUs, autoscaler tried to add but hit account scale caps. Result: queue growth and token throttling. Customer-facing impact: higher latency and partial throttling.
Rebecca (Customer Ops): we already have a handful of enterprise tenants reporting elevated latencies (10–120s on gen endpoints). No errors 5xx yet, mostly timeouts & client-side retries failing.
oncall_tier1: I'm escalating: @Mike can you confirm if we can temporarily bump max_nodes_limit for this cluster? If not, what's fastest workaround?
Mike (Infra): I can request a temporary quota raise but cloud support ETA ~ 30-45m. Faster: we can temporarily reduce autoscaler target to reuse reserved GPUs in other pools and enable manual scale-up of Dedicated pools. Doing manual reassignments will take ~5–10m.
Jonah (Runtime Eng): mitigation plan: 1) revert `max_batch_delay_ms` to previous value (80ms) to restore batching; 2) increase prefix-cache TTL from 3s -> 45s; 3) apply emergency autoscaler override to allow rapid scale to 40 nodes.
Sara (SRE): do them in that order to avoid wasting newly-provisioned nodes while cache coldstart persists.
Aisha (ML Eng): sending config patch for prefix-cache TTL (will patch feature flag `pref_cache.ttl_seconds=45`).
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by Aisha. Patch: `pref_cache.ttl_seconds=45` (change-id: cfg-202404-relative-981). Starting rollout across runtime pods.
Jonah (Runtime Eng): rolling back batching change now. Command:
```
kubectl -n runtime set configmap runtime-batching --from-literal=max_batch_delay_ms=80
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-workers
```
Jonah (Runtime Eng): rollout started, pods terminating/starting. Watch logs.
Sara (SRE): I'm adjusting the routing policy: divert non-critical traffic to lower-cost standby pool to relieve immediate pressure. Executing policy change.
Mike (Infra): manual pool reassignment in progress. Moved 6 reserved GPUs from staging to production standby pool (5–7m to become active).
oncall_tier1: autoscaler override applied: set max_nodes=50 (was 30). This will accept further scale requests immediately. Note recorded in infra-audit.
deploy-bot: runtime deployment cfg-rollback completed at 1716319205. New pods report warm KV cache misses decreasing.
Aisha (ML Eng): prefix-cache TTL patch rolled out; early telemetry: prefix cache hitrate climbing from 42% -> 76% on the critical model shard.
Jonah (Runtime Eng): observed per-worker throughput improving, queue ingress dropping from 12k -> 4.2k in 12 min.
Sara (SRE): monitoring: tail latency 95th p90 dropping from 24s -> 6s for most tenants. Still seeing a few long-running requests from retry storms.
Rebecca (Customer Ops): I posted an interim update to affected customers: we're mitigating, temporary scaling and config changes underway, expect most traffic recovery in ~20–30m. Customers asked for ETA; I've provided 30m and status channel.
Mike (Infra): cloud provider reported initial quota change denied (manual request), but our manual pool moves + autoscaler override should be sufficient. Keeping support ticket open.
Jonah (Runtime Eng): additional small tweak: reduce `min_batch_items=2` -> `4` to favor larger batches where possible, decreasing per-token overhead. Rolling.
Sara (SRE): be careful — increasing min_batch_items can add single-request latency; only apply to background endpoints. Applying selectively.
Jonah (Runtime Eng): applied to non-ephemeral routes. Logs show fewer small batches and better GPU utilization.
oncall_tier1: queue now steady at ~1.1k, autoscaler creating nodes and pods filling them. No more rate-limit errors for scale-controller in recent 5m.
incident-bot: Severity -> mitigated; Pager cleared. Incident duration to this point ~ 46m.
Rebecca (Customer Ops): updating customers: most tenants will see normal behaviour within the hour; offering credits if any SLAs breached. Collecting impacted request IDs.
Sara (SRE): next steps: 1) follow-up postmortem (owner: Sara); 2) revert autoscaler override in 24h unless quota permanently increased; 3) create runbook change to prevent simultaneous low TTL + low batching thresholds from being shipped together.
Aisha (ML Eng): will add a preflight check to config CI to flag combined changes to `pref_cache.ttl_seconds` and `max_batch_delay_ms` for the same deploy.
Mike (Infra): open infra ticket to request permanent quota increase and audit reserved pool assignments. Ticket INFRA-1249.
oncall_tier1: handing off monitoring to the overnight oncall. I'll leave watch for next 2h and then clear.
Sara (SRE): thanks team. Posting incident summary to #postmortems and scheduling a 1h postmortem tomorrow. Preliminary impact: ~8 enterprise tenants affected, tail latency increased 3x–8x, no data loss, no 5xx production errors. Root cause: simultaneous conservative batching change + aggressive cache TTL experiment + autoscaler cap.
Rebecca (Customer Ops): customers notified and follow-up scheduled with CS leads for any compensation discussion.
oncall_tier1: handing off now to night oncall. Leaving runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/batching-cache-incident
Sara (SRE): closing thread, will add links and timelines in postmortem doc. Thanks all.
